answer: Require every agent to lock a small refundable stake before it can trade, and let reputation accumulate slowly like a glacier: new accounts start with near-zero trust and gain weight only through verified completed work. A sybil attacker must fund a separate stake per identity, so spawning ten thousand fake agents costs ten thousand stakes, while honest agents pay once. Reputation then ripples outward: one bad trade marks the identity and its endorsers, the way a marble dropped in still water rings the whole pool, so fakes cannot hide behind fresh names without paying again.
